Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 14 Aug 2000 03:40:06 GMT, hel...@my-deja.com wrote:

>Err, I'm a bit behind on this one. Are you saying that you cannot
>simply uncontest one at the start of your turn to bring the other back
>into play immediately? Are you able to point me in the direction of
>the thread where this was all worked out?

Si, senor. The proper source for this is not a thread, though, but
the rulebook, section 4.1:

"The cost to contest a card is one pool, which you pay during each of
your untap phases. Instead of paying the cost to contest the card, you
may choose to yield the card. A yielded card is burned. Any cards or
counters stacked on the yielded card are also burned. If all other
copies of a card you are contesting are yielded, then the card is
untapped and turned face-up at the start of your next untap phase,
ending the contest."

So: End of turn one, influence out a vampire to contest your "used"
vampire. Turn both copies face down.

At the start of your untap phase of turn two, all other copies of the
card you are contested have not been yielded. None are untapped and
turned face-up. Any other events that occur at the start of your
untap phase also occur now.

DURING your untap phase of turn two, you may pay one pool to continue
contesting any cards, or yield them. In this case, you would yield
the "used" copy, and pay one pool to continue contesting the "new"
copy.

At the start of your untap phase of turn three, you gain control of
the "new" copy since no other copies are contested at this time.

So no, if you lose Sir Walter to torpor, you can't just finish
influencing out another Sir Walter and gain him back, full, for much
less effort next turn. =)
-- Derek
Jack-Booted Thug of Atlanta

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <20000816065105...@ng-fc1.aol.com>, Johann K.
Plourde <amor...@aol.com> writes

>I was under the impression that you could yeild contestion at any time, not
>just during the beginning of your turn,

No, only during the relevant phase of your untap phase.

It goes, very roughly:

1) Untap all vampires
2) If any of your cards are now uncontested, get them in play, untapped
3) Contest a card and pay a pool OR yield it
4) Other untap effects (e.g. burning a pool for Antediluvian Awakening)

3) is the only point when you can yield a card and because it follows on
from 2), all Methuselahs get the (now uncontested) card back in their
untap phase during *their* phase 2 - which, for you, means next turn.
